explanation: A heat engine takes heat Qh from a hot reservoir, converts part of it to useful work W, and must dump the rest as Qc into a cold reservoir — energy conservation forces W = Qh − Qc. The best possible (Carnot) efficiency is η = 1 − Tc/Th, set only by the two reservoir temperatures: a bigger temperature gap means a higher fraction of Qh becomes work. Widen Th versus Tc and watch the green efficiency bar climb and the work arrow grow while less heat trickles to the cold side.
bullets: Energy in must balance: W = Qh − Qc, so you can never turn ALL heat into work.
Carnot efficiency η = 1 − Tc/Th depends only on the reservoir temperatures.
A larger Th/Tc gap means higher efficiency; η = 1 would need Tc = 0 K (impossible).
